title: Support SM90 (Hopper) GPUs in get_bf16_tflops_limit
body:
### Motivation

`get_bf16_tflops_limit()` currently hard-raises on any non-SM100 NVIDIA GPU, so `LLMEngine` (which passes `tflops_limit=get_bf16_tflops_limit() * 2` into the FLOPs estimator, `deepinfer/engine/llm_engine.py:304`) cannot even initialize on SM90 (Hopper) hardware such as H20 — today the most widely deployed inference GPU in mainland China. This is a small, self-contained step toward SM90 support; the heavier items (FlashMLA `sm_90a` target, DeepGEMM FP8/FP32-scale fallbacks for the `fp8_fp4_*` call sites, FP8-expert model variant) are tracked downstream.

### Changes

- `deep_cluster/hardware/nvidia.py`: read the marketing device name via `nvmlDeviceGetName` (same NVML/no-CUDA-context approach as `compute_capability`).
- `deep_cluster/hardware/device.py`: add `is_sm_major_9()` (mirrors `is_sm_major_10()`) and an SM90 branch in `get_bf16_tflops_limit()`. SM90 parts differ ~6.7x in BF16 throughput (H20: 148 vs H100/H800/GH200: 989 TFLOPS dense), so the limit is dispatched on the NVML device-name prefix rather than capability alone; unknown SM90 parts raise with the device name in the message.
- `tests/test_bf16_tflops_limit.py`: mocked unit tests (no GPU required) covering H20 / H20-NVL / H100 / H800 / GH200, unknown-name and missing-name error paths, unchanged SM100 and Ascend behavior.

### Notes

- SM100 and Ascend behavior is unchanged (the SM100 branch is reached before the new SM90 branch).
- `vit.py` already gates on `is_sm_major_10()` with a `cublaslt` fallback, so no other call-site changes are needed for this fix.
